subject: botany
question_text: What are the groups of plants that live as symbionts in lichens? Name the study of lichens.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two symbionts
lines: Algae and fungi live together as symbionts
in lichens. The alga prepares the food; the
fungus provides shelter, water and minerals.
steps.why: The first half asks for the two partner groups; naming both, with one line on what each contributes, shows the symbiosis is understood.
common_mistakes: Naming only one partner — both algae and fungi are required.
Writing bacteria in place of algae — the lichen partners are an alga and a fungus.
steps.memory_tip: Remember the pair by their jobs: alga = food maker, fungus = water, minerals and cover.
steps.margin_note: Two group names plus one line on their roles.

steps.label: Study of lichens

lines.text: The study of lichens is called lichenology.

steps.why: The second half is a single term: add -logy to lichen and the branch name is lichenology.
common_mistakes: Misspelling it 'lichnology' — the full word lichen stays inside lichenology.
Writing mycology — that is the study of fungi alone, not of the lichen partnership.
steps.memory_tip: lichen + ology — the whole word lichen stays inside the branch name.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line answers the second half.

insider_note: Two short asks, two marks: the pair of symbionts and the term lichenology — write both even though each is one line.
